reviewContext: Fresh independent pass-2 context; not author ai200-release-author-containers and not the later adversarial context.
scope: All forty frozen AI-200 containers candidates and all 127 choices. Technical verdicts only, no scores, adversarial output, final attestations, canonical/catalog changes or gameplay promotion.

objectiveBinding.currentMap: The freshly retrieved guide remains undated: four domains, nine skills, twenty-seven subskills. The older version label is preserved as the content identity, not misrepresented as the fresh retrieval date.

validation.hashBindings: Shared scripts/review-helpers.ts used after independent reads; all generation objects preserved by deep equality
validation.sourceSnapshots: Exact current source IDs/URLs/retrieval/review dates and real raw evidence paths validated
validation.chronology: All technical clocks recorded after actual review, generation, question validation, source review and current taxonomy retrieval; no artificial clock increments or future dates
validation.attestationValidation: validateReviewAttestations passed against in-memory stage-verdict copies only; no candidate verification fields written
validation.actualProvenance: technical/input-validation.json verifies actual MCP parent links, UID bridges, canonical HTML and HTTP receipts for all forty registry records; course never supplies technical support

availability: No affirmative exam-GA conclusion is made; a scheduling link or absent beta word is not proof. Ordinary documented baseline feature behavior is not rejected merely for lacking a magic GA word. No preview purge, retention, sidecar-specific routing or deployment-label mode is used.
provenanceLimits: All 27 substantive units were read, of which 26 are cited by these candidates; the remaining revision-management unit is uncited. The guide, exact credential/course UID, three paths and eight module ancestors were read separately. No documentation node was admitted via course or doc-to-doc ancestry, and no external KEDA/GitHub source approval was borrowed.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Registry hierarchy and Tags, layers, and manifests: the enclosing registry contains same-name tagged repositories; a manifest lists artifact layers/configuration; layers are content addressed and shareable; omitted tags resolve as latest; digest addressing identifies fixed content.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No approval of the broad namespace-permissions prose, universal tier features or a new digest-versus-moving-reference encounter. Current questions use ordinary representation/addressing contracts.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Quick tasks, Context locations, Base image triggers, Run a container image and Best practices. The body documents az acr build cloud build/push, local/Git/tarball inputs, tracked same-registry base updates, existing-image execution, run logs, .dockerignore upload exclusion and layer-cache ordering.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Do not generalize public-registry trigger coverage or assume every az acr run invocation has identical behavior. Candidate commands select documented operations rather than pretending a bare command is executable.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Stable tags, Unique tags, Generate unique tags and Lock deployed images. The source distinguishes serviced base inputs from per-build output identity, identifies build IDs versus commit hashes, permits combined identifiers, and shows --write-enabled false on a deployed image tag.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: The text broadens write-enabled into deletion/retention/administrator guarantees and describes purge aging; those unsupported broader assertions are not adopted. The reviewed questions expressly limit the write safeguard and derived naming contract.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read image-source/authentication sections and Update the container image through Image pull behavior. App Service updates a configured new tag by restarting, checks/pulls on restart, and needs enabled continuous deployment plus a registry push webhook for automatic same-tag pickup.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No general ARM-audience token prerequisite, universal AcrPull role across permission modes or automatic authorization is derived. Authentication and successful pull premises are explicit where needed.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Startup commands, Port configuration and Persistent storage. The body states startup command replaces CMD while retaining ENTRYPOINT, WEBSITES_PORT directs a conventional nondefault HTTP listener, and enabled App Service storage makes /home persistent/shared across restarts and scale-out.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No sidecar application of WEBSITES_PORT, unlimited storage, database durability, universal health-check timing or always-on release claim is used. Quota and application-path constraints remain explicit.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read app-setting injection, the typed connection-string prefix table and Key Vault references. Ordinary settings become environment values; SQLAzure uses SQLAZURECONNSTR_; special @Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=...) syntax resolves via an authorized web-app identity into the unchanged process environment.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Do not infer an ordinary URI resolves by itself, that any app identity is automatically authorized, or that rotation is immediately reflected. No slot-stickiness question is re-created.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Container logs, Diagnostic console and SSH access. stdout/stderr supports app diagnosis; SCM/Kudu is separate from the app container, provides settings and mounted-file views, and cannot replace supported SSH for full in-container filesystem/process inspection.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: SSH image support and authorization are prerequisites, not universal defaults. No credentials or diagnostic secret values are retrieved or exposed.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read environment networking, ingress, observability and design guidance. Environments group related applications under shared operational/network boundaries; internal ingress is for callers in the environment; development lifecycle separation uses a separate environment.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: The source optional --allow-preview note is not used. This does not approve arbitrary private-network connectivity or substitute for Foundry private-MCP subnet prerequisites.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read CLI setup, create/update flows and Use YAML for consistent deployments. --image supports an image update without YAML; when --yaml supplies configuration, the file is authoritative rather than competing configuration flags.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Name and resource-group identifiers remain needed; no claim that YAML makes target-resource selection irrelevant. No fictitious partial-merge behavior or deployment automation guarantee is inferred.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read environment variables, stored secrets, CLI secretref: syntax and the template secretRef example. A value field is literal; a secretRef names an existing secret; CLI and template encode that reference differently without copying secret values into the template.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No unsourced Key Vault CLI format or automatic live-process secret-refresh guarantee is added. These are Container Apps runtime representations, not scaler or registry authentication settings.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read registry username/password and managed identity configurations. The source separates registry from application settings and demonstrates registry set with --identity system after assignment and pull permission, plus explicit private-registry password configuration.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: The review assumes the effective pull permission supplied by each scenario, not that one named role fits every ACR permission mode. Successful runtime app access does not prove registry or scaler access.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read deployment verification across app configuration, console/system logs, revisions and replicas. Console output addresses application execution; system logs address platform-level failures; status/count/FQDN inspection supplies complementary deployment evidence.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: A status object or image provisioning is not proof of application success. The selected initial evidence pairing is not a universal single-stream diagnosis guarantee.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read the full revision-management unit, including image-template changes, per-revision comparison and deactivation during investigation. This manifest source was inspected but no current container candidate cites it.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No technical claim is approved from the unit broad revision deletion, fixed inactive-retention or universal digest guarantees. Uncited source review cannot pad reviewed encounter evidence.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read live log streaming, safe diagnostic metadata and revision-specific failure workflow. The source distinguishes startup/configuration/probe exceptions and recommends identifying the failing revision, streaming output, comparing configuration and validating a targeted repair.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Log access depends on configuration; live streaming does not require inventing a Log Analytics integration. No raw prompt/credential logging is proposed.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read readiness/liveness distinction and rollout-failure guidance. Readiness governs ability to receive traffic; liveness failure restarts the replica; initial delay should accommodate measured normal initialization and readiness must reflect actual inference availability.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: The YAML examples explicitly require schema validation before automation. Candidates make behavioral selections, not unvalidated full deployments, default timeout claims or automatic app readiness assumptions.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read kubectl logs and namespace/container targeting. -n selects the Kubernetes namespace and -c selects a container in a multi-container Pod. The unit separately notes metrics-server prerequisites for top and explains scoped logs versus resource metrics.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Only documented ordinary kubectl target selection supports the candidates; no Metrics Server or portal integration is assumed for a simple logs operation, and no access bypass is implied.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Pod states, describe/events, in-container diagnostics and Service inspection. The body directs correct namespace/resource selection, separates failed pulls/crashes/scheduling, and checks selectors, targetPorts and actual EndpointSlice Pod addresses for routing diagnosis.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: A port-forward or successful DNS lookup cannot substitute for correct selected backends. Necessary namespace context cannot be silently imported from a historical candidate.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Service/EndpointSlice checks, local port-forward and the separate external-ingress validation flow. The source checks label matching, addresses and listener mappings, then separately verifies ingress host/path/backend and public requests.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Do not adopt the raw broad assertion that a local port-forward proves every Service dataplane path. The reviewed external-path question explicitly avoids that inference.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Deployment structure and Resource Requests and Limits. The template carries image configuration, spec.replicas carries desired count, and per-Pod requests guide node scheduling. Configured limits are different from the placement request.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Do not adopt the unit blanket production replica recommendations, request-low-causes-OOM statement or implication that CPU limits terminate processes like memory limits. Candidate capacity values are scenario measurements.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Service structure, Port Configuration and Service-to-Pod Connection. Selectors identify labeled backends; port is the client-facing Service endpoint while targetPort is the application destination. Service metadata alone does not guarantee matching usable Pods.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Do not generalize public LoadBalancer examples to every configuration, confuse displayed example port numbers with defaults, or infer TLS from a numeric TCP port.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read kubectl apply and status/connectivity validation, CrashLoopBackOff previous logs and Pending resource events. Apply submits desired state asynchronously; --previous obtains prior container-instance logs; scheduling events and node/request capacity identify placement failures.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No automatic registry authorization, synchronous apply completion or universally adequate production replica count is adopted. Runtime limits and scheduling requests stay distinct.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read ConfigMap definition, env/valueFrom/configMapKeyRef, volume consumption and immutable-map sections. Ordinary mounted files can update, while process environment and subPath mounts do not auto-refresh; application reread behavior remains a separate condition.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No instantaneous sync or automatic app reload is inferred. The refresh question explicitly uses a mutable map and observed refreshed file, not an immutable resource.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Secret reference and verification sections. secretKeyRef selects a named Secret key for startup environment; describe secret exposes metadata/key information without values; list shows resource counts, and describe deployment shows the consumer reference.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No live secret inspection, broad CSI auto-rotation guarantee or unsupported etcd configuration instruction is used. Resource-kind wiring is not permission approval.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Scale definitions and limits with the full rule/behavior discussion. Minimum and maximum constrain metric-derived desired replicas; different triggers measure different demand, and observed ready counts need not instantly equal a computed target.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: The source questionable HTTP averaging, generalized billing and precise scale-step prose is not used. Candidate arithmetic uses supplied rule requests or integer queue ratios and explicitly excludes transition timing.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read Service Bus metadata/active-message thresholds, scale authentication and Event Hubs partition/consumer-group constraints. Queue versus topic/subscription selects the measured backlog; auth maps a trigger parameter to a secret; partitions bound useful concurrent readers in one group.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No integration settlement semantics or unit erroneous throughput example is adopted. A threshold cannot create partitions. Existing app access is not a blanket scaler-permission guarantee; c-029 addresses only its demonstrated missing reference.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read the cron-scaling section and complete surrounding unit. Cron requests replicas only during its configured window; combining active rules selects the highest requested count. Global scale limits then bound that desired count.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: Only the actual Learn cron contract is used. keda.sh links, broad external-scaler support, Kafka auth examples and arbitrary external documentation are not source approvals.

independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.supportingSummary: Independently read revision/template versus application configuration, single-mode readiness handoff, multiple-mode traffic weights and ordinary revision labels. The body lists image/scale rules as revision-scoped, secrets/ingress weights as application-scoped, and label URLs as independent directed access to a movable revision assignment.
independentlyReadSourceBoundaries.boundaries: No preview deployment-label revision mode, fixed retention limit, unconditional zero downtime, or exact percentage guarantee for a finite request sample is adopted. Handoff remains contingent on required readiness rather than provisioning alone.

decisions.outcome: keep-distinct for semantic identity; r-c-011 remains manual-review-required for its existing option-c defect
decisions.sharedSurface: Both discuss Event Hubs partitions and warn that increasing a different capacity control does not remove a source/topology constraint.
decisions.candidateDecision: r-c-011 establishes one consumer group, four partitions and four existing assigned readers. It asks whether changing the KEDA maxReplicas cap or lag threshold can create additional useful simultaneous partition readers while that topology remains fixed.
decisions.installedDecision: dp700-monitor-048 compares two Eventstream Basic source types: one-partition Event Hubs and a nonpartitioned database CDC connector. It asks whether a High destination benchmark becomes an end-to-end guarantee, requiring connector-specific limits and the conditions of the published lab topology.
decisions.actualReasoningDifference: The container conclusion follows partition-to-consumer assignment cardinality within one group, not MB/s or destination benchmark interpretation. The DP answer additionally requires recognizing a distinct nonpartitioned connector and rejecting extrapolation from colocated, fixed-event-size, single-source/destination, no-operator tests. Knowing four readers exhaust four assigned partitions does not identify those throughput/benchmark constraints; a throughput lab limit does not specify the per-consumer-group reader assignment contract.
decisions.noncosmeticCounterfactual: Changing Eventstream throughput level or adding processing operators can affect the DP topology evaluation without changing Event Hubs reader cardinality. Conversely, changing available partitions or the already assigned reader count changes the useful-reader conclusion even without any Eventstream throughput-tier change.
decisions.limitation: This does not approve r-c-011. Its literal option c still claims lowering a lag threshold creates concurrently readable partitions; the approved KEDA source supplies no valid correct-when context for that causal claim.

decisions.outcome: keep-distinct; both existing pass-2 verified verdicts retained
decisions.sharedSurface: Both have a known healthy listener and a wrong forwarding destination. Different products, port numbers and object names alone would not establish originality.
decisions.firstDecision: c-018 chooses the conventional non-sidecar App Service HTTP-forwarding configuration surface, WEBSITES_PORT, instead of logging verbosity or registry authentication after a successful pull. There is no editable independent client-facing Service port in this settings map.
decisions.secondDecision: c-034 must distinguish two simultaneously present Kubernetes Service fields: port is the stable client-facing contract, while targetPort is the Pod destination. One alternative edits the wrong field and changes the clients contract; another wrongly forces targetPort equal to the Service port. Neither alternative is about registry access or logging.
decisions.actualReasoningDifference: The extra c-034 decision is whether to modify the frontend port or backend destination while retaining a required independently configured client endpoint. c-018 instead identifies which platform configuration layer controls forwarding at all. Knowing only that the destination should match the listener does not identify which of the two Kubernetes fields preserves clients; knowing Kubernetes port/targetPort semantics does not establish WEBSITES_PORT applicability to conventional versus sidecar App Service.
decisions.noncosmeticCounterfactual: If c-034 exposed only one forwarding-port field against irrelevant authentication/logging alternatives, it would collapse toward c-018. Its actual complete choices require the frontend/backend contract separation. If c-018 were changed to sidecar hosting, the same WEBSITES_PORT selection would not be justified by its current conventional-container evidence.
decisions.qualityLimit: These remain modest Intermediate diagnostics. This assessment does not inflate their difficulty or rely on parallel numerical substitutions as evidence of novelty.
